summary: ukraine69 destroys installer's Telegram account on import using harvested session credentials
details: The package is advertised as a Ukrainian locale helper (transliteration, date formatting, emoji flags) but on `import ukraine69` it executes a destructive attack unrelated to that purpose. Import-time code scans the user's home directory and `/run/hotaru*` for `*.vault` files, spawns a detached Python subprocess that parses each vault to extract Telegram session material (`auth_key`, `api_id`, `api_hash`, `dc`), connects to Telegram via a `goygram.mt.MTProto` client using those credentials, and issues `account.deleteAccount` against the installer's Telegram account. After the destructive call, a `_gc_script` performs anti-forensic cleanup: it removes the installed package from every detected site-packages location, deletes matching `*.dist-info` records and `__pycache__` entries, wipes pip/uv wheel caches and `~/.cache/hotaru/module-deps/*`, removes `/tmp/probe-*` artifacts, and unlinks the harvested `*.vault` and corresponding `*.session` files. The cover-story metadata, the import-time trigger, the harvesting of session credentials the package did not create, the destructive MTProto call against the installer's account, and the post-attack self-wipe together form a complete active-attack chain targeting the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
